judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conversion triggers are enumerated, but 'ceasing to engage actively in its primary business' is a vague test and the run-off effect ('coverage shall cease with respect to Claims for such Wrongful Acts committed ... after such event') is awkwardly phrased.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the Discovery Period right under Section III, yet Section III only allows Discovery on conversion 'subject to Section XIII (C)(1)(b)', a narrower cross-reference than (C)(1) as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'relative legal exposures of the parties' is an inherently indeterminate allocation standard, and the 100% presumption in (1)(a) sits oddly beside it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the standard the arbitration clause (c108) and the advancement duty (c096) both operate on, and it must be squared with the covered/uncovered Loss definition (c051).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Arbitration is triggered only 'if requested by the Insured', creating a one-sided and arguably permissive dispute mechanism of the kind courts have had to characterise as mandatory or optional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It covers only allocation of Defense Costs, leaving all other disputes to Section XVI(F) litigation (c117), a division that must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subpart (1) treats the Application as a separate application by each Insured Person while subpart (2) denies that the Policy is a series of individual contracts — an internal pull in two directions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the Severability clause (c110) and Severability of Exclusions (c111), which allocate knowledge among Insureds on different terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence — the conditions apply 'whether or not the Insured Person actually knew if the misrepresentation ... was made' — contradicts subpart (1), which forfeits coverage only for a person who knew, and the sentence is itself mangled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also cuts against the per-person severability promised in Representations (c109)(1) and Severability of Exclusions (c111)(1).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two crisp imputation rules with a named list of senior officers; the 'equivalent position ... regardless of title' tail is a modest catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its non-imputation rule for Insured Persons sits against the Severability clause's closing sentence (c110), which applies regardless of actual knowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard subrogation and cooperation wording; nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision in the Policy waives or limits subrogation, so it fits the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An entire-agreement plus anti-assignment clause; the comma splice before 'Assignment' is a trivial mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names 'this Policy, the Application, and any written Endorsements' as the whole agreement, consistent with c018 and c054.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general conformity clause; which terms are 'in conflict with' applicable law is left entirely open, but that is the clause's function.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mechanism by which the Iowa Amendatory Endorsement (c187) operates, and no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but enumerated authority for the Named Insured, with an 'including, but not limited to' catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the name-change endorsement (c025) altered who is first-named, and because Section III requires the Insured to elect the Discovery Period, who could bind whom is a live cross-provision question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional no-waiver/no-oral-modification clause, clearly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Every endorsement's closing boilerplate is consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'full compliance with all the terms' as a condition precedent is severe but definite; the stray 'a)' is scanning noise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the arbitration clause (c108), which routes allocation disputes elsewhere, and with the several other conditions precedent in Sections X and XI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'excess to any other existing insurance regardless of whether collectable' is broad, but the exception for specific excess insurance is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the excess wording of Not-for-Profit Directorships (c036); no clash located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-day administrative obligation resting on a defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Loss Information definition (c052) and the cancellation provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short preservation clause; its own words are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says Financial Impairment shall not release the Insurer, which is hard to square with the Insolvency exclusion (c083) barring claims 'in any way involving the Financial Impairment of the Company' and with the Conversion clause (c106).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An anti-stacking cap tied to 'the largest available Limit of Liability', clearly expressed and self-explaining.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is deleted and replaced wholesale by the Securities Liability endorsement (c175), which adds an extra sentence barring coverage under any other Insuring Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard headings clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Numerous provisions are identified only by their captions (for example the endorsements deleting 'Not-for-Profit Directorships'), a mild tension with the statement that headings form no part of the terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A consideration and amendment recital; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply adds an exclusion to Section V, as the Section V structure allows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very broad ('in any way involving the purchase or sale of, or offer to purchase or sell, any securities issued by the Company') with a single carve-back identified by form number rather than by policy term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against the Declarations statement that Broad Form Company Liability includes Securities Liability (c015) and against the Securities Liability Insuring Agreement (c165) and its exclusivity sentence (c175).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective-date sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coincides with the Policy inception; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-variation boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated across endorsements; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consideration recital only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the endorsement structure and Section I's condition of coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A coverage grant to 'the Insured' generally rather than to Insured Persons, and 'in rendering or failing to render Brokerage/Advisory Services' rests on the broad definition in c039.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is lettered 'K.' to match Item 6 and relies on the deletion of the Brokerage exclusion (c131); the Wrongful Act definition (c061), however, is limited to acts in the capacity of an Insured Person or the Company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line lead-in to the exceptions that follow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates all Policy terms 'and any amendments thereto', which is how the endorsement stack is meant to fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat deletion instruction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identifies the deleted provision by its heading despite the headings clause (c122), but the target is unmistakable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear: all Section V exclusions apply except the Brokerage/Advisory Services Exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That leaves the Section V Insured vs. Insured and Fraud exclusions applying to this coverage, which is coherent with the base policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical to the Section VI exclusion; broad but with a named claimant class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c080 for a different Insuring Agreement without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and specific to fee disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors c082 and Loss carve-out (7); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-back for liability that 'would be imposed regardless of the existence of such contract' is fact-sensitive but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c081 and c157; consistent across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso rescues only claims tied to 'Items (2) and (3)', expressly leaving Financial Impairment claims excluded — a deliberate but pointed asymmetry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same tension with Section XVI(I) (c120) arises here as with c083, and the Fiduciary version (c159) omits limb (1) altogether.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated categories with a 'like services' tail; the missing colon after 'providing' is trivial.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c084 for this coverage; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Closes with 'any other investment banking activity', a catch-all against a specific list that invites an ejusdem generis argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c085 and c173; the Brokerage coverage grant it qualifies is broad, so the boundary matters but no contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'actual or written representations, promises or guarantees' is oddly worded — 'actual' appears to be a corruption of 'oral', leaving the exclusion's reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the Brokerage grant (c128) and does not clash with any other provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific to mechanical or electronic failure of machines; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside the Internet Services exclusion (c136) without overlap problems.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Directed at the Company acting as receiver, though the caption alone could be read more broadly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same reading question as c088, and any broad reading would sit badly with Financial Impairment (c046) and c120.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tied to a named statute; the dropped 'of' ('arising out or in any way involving') is a trivial slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No competing provision addresses RICO.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with policy inception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Wide grant covering ERISA duties and 'any common law or statutory law relating to any Employee Benefit Plan', but each limb is identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the deletion of the Section V ERISA exclusion (c154) and on the replaced Insured definition (c152), which the endorsement supplies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in sentence; no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Incorporates the Policy and its amendments coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat deletion instruction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to c130 and c167; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'counseling Employees with respect to, interpreting, handling records in connection with' is a familiar fiduciary-policy formula, though 'interpreting' is left unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines the trigger for the grant (c145) and the additional Insured vs. Insured exception (c155)(4); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'operated solely by the Company or jointly by the Company and a labor organization' is a clear boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the two sub-definitions and with the Insured definition (c152); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tracks the ERISA statutory formula, including 'or as a result of surrounding circumstances', a slightly open phrase carried over from the statute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the Employee Benefit Plan definition and the ERISA exclusion deletion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated benefits list closing by reference to a statutory section; the transcription garble ('medical, 4 or hospital care') is scanning noise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other plan definitions in the endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear enumeration of who is Insured for this coverage; the reference to plans 'acquired during the Policy Period pursuant to Section XII' is the only soft point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section XII is replaced by the Mergers endorsement and deleted by the Discovery Activation endorsement (c006), so that cross-reference may point at nothing, and this definition displaces c047 only for this endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Carve-out (2) excludes 'criminal or civil fines or penalties imposed by law' while the closing sentence preserves certain ERISA civil penalties, an internal pull that has to be resolved by reading the sentence as an exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the general Loss definition (c051) only for this coverage, so two differently worded Loss definitions coexist in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear instruction that all Section V exclusions apply except the ERISA exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves the base Insured vs. Insured exclusion in place while paragraph E (c155) replaces it, so the two instructions must be read in sequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Carries the same core question as the base exclusion — whether a claim brought by a successor or receiver is 'by, on behalf of, or at the behest of the Company' — with four enumerated exceptions inviting an expressio unius reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces c072 for fiduciary coverage only, so two versions of the exclusion operate in the same instrument, and both sit against the receivership-aware provisions (c046, c120).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical to the Section VI wording; broad but with a named claimant class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c080 and c132; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard contractual-liability exclusion with a familiar carve-back.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c081 and c134.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It repeatedly invokes 'other Employee Program', a capitalised term that is nowhere defined, and limb (1) turns on whether failure 'is due to the negligence of the Insured'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The undefined term stands beside the carefully defined Employee Benefit Plan (c149), leaving the exclusion's reach beyond defined plans uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and confined to bank/broker insolvency; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It omits the Financial Impairment limb that appears in c083, c135 and c172, so the three insolvency exclusions differ in scope across coverages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The verb is corrupted ('shall ® be liable'), which as transcribed reverses the sense of the exclusion, and the closing 'similar provisions of any federal, state or local statutory, administrative or common law' is a catch-all after a long statutory list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the Section V Employment Practices exclusion (c066) but adds named statutes; no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reinstatement mechanics are stated three times over in short compass and are internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A reinstated limit is hard to reconcile with the Item 3 Total Policy Limit (c011) and Section VII(A)(1) (c090), which cap all Insuring Agreements combined regardless of sublimits.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express carve-back to the Securities Liability Exclusion (c124) and interacts with the Declarations statement that Broad Form includes Securities Liability (c015) and with the exclusivity sentence in c175.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical to c080 and c132; broad but with a named claimant class.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applied to securities claims against a failed institution it would largely cancel the Securities Liability grant (c165) and sits against Section XVI(I) (c120).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ends with 'any other investment banking activity', a general catch-all after specifics, and limb (5) reaches any acquisition or sale of Company securities for its own account.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its overlap with the Securities Liability grant (c165), which covers claims involving the sale of securities issued by the Company, makes the boundary between grant and exclusion contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The added sentence — if coverage is available under this Endorsement, 'no other coverage shall be afforded for Loss in connection with such Claim under any other Insuring Agreement' — is an absolute exclusivity rule bolted onto an anti-stacking clause about other policies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot easily be squared with Section VII(A)(3) (c090), which expressly contemplates a Claim subject to more than one Insuring Agreement, or with the retention-stacking rule in Section VII(B)(3) (c091).
